document.executive_summary: Civic Water Engineering must select one pump module for its water-reclamation transfer loop. Four anonymous candidates were assessed against the supplied policy: qualify with a quality index of at least 80 and no more than 5 raw defects, then take the qualifying module with the lowest measured energy on the common acceptance run. All four candidates clear both gates. Measured energy spans 12 to 58 kWh. P2 dominates the deciding metric at 12 kWh, 40 kWh below the next-lowest qualifier, P3, and it also carries the highest quality index (97) with a single recorded defect. The other three qualifiers cluster within 6 kWh of one another, so they are nearly interchangeable on energy. recommendation.rationale: P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying candidate at 12 kWh, 40 kWh below runner-up P3, while also holding the highest quality index (97) with only one recorded defect. All four candidates pass both policy gates, so the energy rule decides, and P2's margin dwarfs every supplied nuance. Caveats: cost, delivery and field data are absent, and the ranking深度

sections.body: All four candidates clear both policy gates. Quality indices are P1 84, P2 97, P3 80, P4 81: every value meets the minimum of 80, with P3 sitting exactly at the threshold. Raw defect counts are P1 4, P2 1, P3 3, P4 0: all within the maximum of 5, and P4 records none. No candidate is eliminated, so the ranking decision falls entirely to the energy criterion. One fragility is worth noting: P3's exact-threshold quality leaves zero tolerance for any future measurement revision, since a one-point drop would disqualify it outright.
sections.heading: 1. Qualification Screening Against Both PolicyG

sections.body: Measured energy on the shared acceptance run is P2 12 kWh, P3 52, P1 56, P4 58. P2 leads by 40 kWh over P3, roughly 77% below the runner-up and well under the qualifier average of 44.5 kWh. The three slower modules sit close together: P3 to P1 is 4 kWh and P1 to P4 is 2 kWh, so they are nearly interchangeable on this metric, whereas P2 is a clear outlier. Under the policy's minimize-energy rule, P2 is the unambiguous qualifying winner regardless of how any residual ties would be broken.
sections.heading: 2. Energy Ranking and Gap Analysis

sections.body: P2 pairs the lowest energy with the strongest quality index (97) and a single defect, so no quality is sacrificed to obtain the energy saving. P4 offers a zero-defect build but the highest energy at 58 kWh, 46 kWh above P2. P1 and P3 carry more defects (4 and 3) and higher energy, and P3's threshold-level quality adds fragility. If the client valued defect-free assembly alone, P4 would merit attention, but the stated policy makes energy the deciding metric once the gates are passed, and P4 trails P2 by 46 kWh.
sections.heading: 3. Quality-Defect Trade-offs

sections.body: Several inputs were not supplied and remain unverified: unit cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden, and field reliability beyond the single acceptance run. One measurement per candidate cannot reveal variability, wear or degradation over time. Cost-per-kWh comparisons, spares strategy and vendor responsiveness therefore cannot be ranked from this record. Before final procurement, request costed quotes and reliability history for P2 and the runner-up P3, and confirm the acceptance-run duty matches the actual transfer-loop duty. None of these open questions changes the ranking under the supplied policy.

body.figure_brief: Supporting job illustration for the WO-01 pump-module decision report. Show a water-reclamation transfer loop receiving a selected pump module. On one side, a four-bar chart of measured acceptance-run energy (P1 56, P2 12, P3 52, P4 58 kWh) with P2 highlighted as the lowest-energy qualifying module; on the other side, a schematic loop with tank, pump module and transfer line, and a check-mark badge on the selected module. Include small labels: quality index and defect count for each candidate (P1 84/4, P2 97/1, P3 80/3, P4 81/0), the policy gates (quality ≥ 80, defects ≤ 5), and the energy gap P2 over P3 of 40 kWh. Clean industrial-technical style, readable serif labels, muted blue-gray palette with one accent color for P2.
